citations.quote: DUBAI AGENTS ARE SCAMMERS." A client told me this. This week.

situation.text: A client described Dubai agents as scammers in a conversation this week.

citations.quote: I’ve seen around 50 tactics in my career - selling myself, then coaching agents to sell. Some work. Some work sometimes. Most are old. Swipe for the 5 that get you ghosted

observation.text: The text introduces the topic by stating the author's experience with various tactics and then promises to reveal ineffective ones that cause 'ghosting'.

citations.quote:
1
OPENING WITH PRESSURE
"It's the last unit. First come, first serve. The price will go up."

2
ASKING ONLY ABOUT THE BUDGET "No one bedroom for that. Only studios."

observation.text: A numbered list format is used to categorize different sales tactics that are deemed ineffective, each with brief examples and outcomes.

citations.quote: Clients stop responding to you and you don't know why. You're probably using one of these old tactics that makes you feel like a scammer to them.

summary.text: Some real estate tactics used by agents are outdated and can make agents seem dishonest to clients.

citations.quote: OPENING WITH PRESSURE "It's the last unit. First come, first serve. The price will go up."

summary.text: Opening interactions by pressuring clients with scarcity and urgency statements such as 'It's the last unit' can be seen as a scam.

citations.quote: ASKING ONLY ABOUT THE BUDGET "No one bedroom for that. Only studios." You learned one thing about him and used it against him. He will never open up.

summary.text: Asking clients only about their budget and then using that information to limit their options can prevent them from sharing more information.

knowledge.title: Tactic: Asking Only About the Budget

citations.quote: ASKING FOR AN OFFER THE OWNER ALREADY DECLINED You just told him the owner said no to that price. Now you want him to offer it.

summary.text: Encouraging clients to make offers that the owner has already declined can be counterproductive.

citations.quote: PUSHING YOUR STOCK He told you the layout, the size, what he wants. You send him whatever is available. He knows you're pushing your stock.

summary.text: When agents push whatever stock they have rather than what aligns with the client's needs, it can damage trust.

citations.quote: WOBBLING ON THE NUMBERS Square footage. Price per square foot. Layout. You go vague on the numbers of your own project — and it sounds like a scam to him.

summary.text: Being vague about important numbers, like square footage or price per square foot, can be perceived as dishonest.
